narrative_purpose: Shows the forest as a connected food web rather than isolated pairs, so the reader can see how pressure from an apex predator at the top reaches down through links to animals it never touches.
subject: A vertical ecological hierarchy of luminous animal silhouettes against deep indigo. At the apex, the great winged leonopteryx with expansive glowing wing membranes. Below it, intermediate winged banshees and stingbats. Beneath them, a central cluster of small arboreal and terrestrial herbivores including hexapedes and prolemuris. Near the forest floor, a pack of sleek viperwolves, and anchored at the base, a solitary massive thanator. The silhouettes are linked by delicate, natural filaments of bioluminescent light.
scene: An abstract celestial-style biological map showing the trophic tiers of a Pandoran rainforest against deep indigo darkness.
camera: Flat head-on naturalist cutaway view of the vertical web.
light: Self-luminous silhouettes and connecting threads against dark; no external light.
palette: Void-indigo ground, cyan and living-teal silhouettes, a single scarce warm magenta glint on the top apex flyer to draw the eye, threads pale stone-grey.
style: Painterly plate that reads as a wiring diagram through composition alone, soft glowing forms, not a hard vector chart.
detail_level: Moderate: silhouettes simple and clearly different in scale, the top-to-bottom link structure obvious.
composition: Vertical hierarchy across the frame, apex predator at top, intermediate predators in middle tiers, herbivores and terrestrial apex below, framed by deep negative space.
consistency_notes: Creature silhouettes echo the chapter's earlier figures (apex flyer, pack predator, massive ground predator, six-legged grazers). Reads as a teaching specimen study.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no tick marks, no arrows, no grid, no diagram chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look
